newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo buys rest of Japanese joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo buys rest of Japanese joint venture.

text.p: British pharmaceutical giant Glaxo Wellcome Plc said on Thursday it was buying the outstanding 50 percent of its Japanese joint venture Nippon Glaxo Ltd for 66 billion yen, or 354 million pounds ($595 million).
Glaxo Wellcome said its current partner in Nippon Glaxo, privately-owned Shin Nihon Jitsuggo Co Ltd (SNJ), would also receive 1.38 billion yen, or 7.4 million pounds, in lieu of dividend for 1996.

Glaxo, which said it expected the move to enhance its earnings, said taking full management control of Nippon Glaxo would give it a platform to make the most of Glaxo Wellcome's business in Japan, the world's second largest pharmaceutical market.

Hiroshi Konishi, president of Nippon Glaxo, and Akira Konishi, vice-president and general manager, would give up these positions but remain members of Nippon Glaxo's board, the Glaxo Wellcome statement said.
Nippon Glaxo, which develops, makes and markets prescription drugs in Japan, had net assets at June 30 of 30.7 billion yen, or 180 million pounds.
Its profits after tax for the six months ended June 30 were 2.5 billion yen, 15.6 million pounds. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717 ($1=.5950 Pound)
